You can also add ELSE to IF-ELSE IF block. Try to form the IF-ELSE IF-ELSE block from the IF block.
Referring to the image below, the program will check in this sequence:
  1. It will check from the top.
  2. If Condition 1 is True, then Code A will run and after running, it will skip the rest of the block.
  3. If Condition 1 is False, it will then check Condition 2. If Condition 2 is True, Code B will run and after running, it will skip the rest of the block.
  4. If Conditions 1 & 2 are False, it will then check Condition 3. If Condition 3 is True, Code C will run and after running, it will skip the rest of the block.
  5. If all the Conditions are False, it will run Code D.
   

Note that it is optional to have an ELSE in the IF block. When there is no ELSE and all conditions are False, then no codes will be run.


You are creating a steering control for a racing game that does the following:
1. When Button D18 is pressed, display "turn left".
2. When Button D22 is pressed, display "turn right".
3. When no buttons are pressed, display "move forward".
